<!-- Generated by `ims gen docs` from the Cobra command tree (internal/cli). Do not edit: run `make docs-gen`. -->

The binary is the CLI. In development run commands from source with `go run ./cmd/app <command>`;
a built binary runs them as `ims <command>`. Global flags work with every command.
To add your own command, see [CLI commands](../guides/cli-commands.md).

## Global flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--env-file` | — | path to the env file (default: APP_ENV_FILE or .env) |
| `--verbose` | — | enable debug logging |

### activity:prune

Delete activity-log entries older than --days (default ACTIVITY_RETENTION_DAYS, at least 30).

```bash
ims activity:prune [flags]
```

Examples:

```bash
ims activity:prune --days=90
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--days` | `0` | delete entries older than this many days (default: ACTIVITY_RETENTION_DAYS, at least 30) |

### backup:clean

Apply the retention policy to stored backups.

```bash
ims backup:clean [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--dry-run` | — | report what would be deleted without deleting |

### backup:list

List recent backup runs.

```bash
ims backup:list [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--limit` | `20` | maximum runs to list |

### backup:monitor

Check backup freshness and storage usage.

```bash
ims backup:monitor
```

### backup:run

Create a database backup archive.

```bash
ims backup:run [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--destinations` | — | comma-separated destinations (local is always included) |
| `--filename` | — | archive filename override |
| `--with-files` | — | include BACKUP_FILES_PATHS in the archive |

### delivery:test

Send one message now (not queued) to --to: an e-mail address for mail, a phone number
(E.164) for sms, a user id for push. Without --template a plain test message is sent;
with one, the template is rendered with its sample data.

```bash
ims delivery:test [flags]
```

Examples:

```bash
ims delivery:test --to=you@example.com
ims delivery:test --to=you@example.com --template=password-reset --locale=bn
ims delivery:test --channel=sms --to=+8801712345678 --template=otp-code
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--channel` | `mail` | mail \| sms \| push |
| `--locale` | — | template locale, e.g. bn (default: APP_FALLBACK_LOCALE) |
| `--template` | — | template to render with its sample data (default: a plain test message) |
| `--to` | — | recipient: e-mail (mail), E.164 phone (sms) or user id (push) |

### dev-dashboard:prune


### down

Put the application into maintenance mode: every API process answers 503 MAINTENANCE_MODE
within MAINTENANCE_CHECK_INTERVAL. /up, /api/health, /metrics, /dev and /docs keep working;
a client sending the bypass secret in the X-Maintenance-Bypass header passes.

```bash
ims down [flags]
```

Examples:

```bash
ims down --message="Upgrading the database" --retry=120 --with-secret
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--message` | — | message shown to API clients (default: "The service is down for maintenance. Please try again shortly.") |
| `--retry` | `60` | Retry-After hint in seconds |
| `--secret` | — | bypass secret clients may send in the X-Maintenance-Bypass header |
| `--with-secret` | — | generate a bypass secret and print it once |

### feature-flags:sync

Insert missing global feature flags with their catalog defaults.

```bash
ims feature-flags:sync
```

### gen docs

Render docs/reference/{cli,configuration,permissions,make}.md from the code: the
command tree, .env.example, the permission catalog and the Makefile. With --check
nothing is written and the command fails when a committed page is stale (CI).

```bash
ims gen docs [flags]
```

Examples:

```bash
ims gen docs
ims gen docs --check
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--check` | — | fail when a generated page is stale instead of writing it |
| `--root` | `.` | repository root |

### gen module

Generate a goose migration, sqlc queries and a feature-first module package
from a field spec. Non-interactive and CI-friendly.

```bash
ims gen module [flags]
```

Examples:

```bash
ims gen module --name=product --fields="name:string,price:decimal,is_active:bool"
ims gen module --name=product --fields="name:string,notes:text?" --dry-run
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--dry-run` | — | print the files without writing them |
| `--fields` | — | comma-separated name:type spec, e.g. name:string,notes:text? |
| `--force` | — | overwrite existing files |
| `--module` | — | go module path (default: read from go.mod) |
| `--name` | — | module name, lower_snake, singular (required) |
| `--no-openapi` | — | skip refreshing the generated OpenAPI regions |
| `--no-sqlc` | — | skip the automatic `sqlc generate` step |
| `--package` | — | go package name (default: --name) |
| `--root` | `.` | repository root |
| `--table` | — | table name (default: naive plural of --name) |

### gen openapi

Insert or update the generated paths and schemas for one module
(--module), every module in the index (--all), or insert the empty marker
regions (--init). Managed regions are owned by the tool; everything
outside the markers is hand-written and never touched.

```bash
ims gen openapi [flags]
```

Examples:

```bash
ims gen openapi --init
ims gen openapi --module=product
ims gen openapi --all --check
ims gen openapi --all --dry-run
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--all` | — | refresh every module listed in the generated-region index |
| `--check` | — | exit non-zero when the committed regions are stale |
| `--dry-run` | — | print the regenerated regions without writing |
| `--init` | — | insert the empty managed regions (one-time) |
| `--module` | — | refresh a single module (lower_snake name) |
| `--root` | `.` | repository root |

### health:check

Run application health checks.

```bash
ims health:check
```

### key:generate

Generate a random APP_KEY and write it to the .env file. APP_KEY encrypts values the
app must read back (two-factor secrets, sensitive job payloads). Replacing a key that is
in use makes those values unreadable: move the old key to APP_PREVIOUS_KEYS first.

```bash
ims key:generate [flags]
```

Examples:

```bash
ims key:generate
ims key:generate --show
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--force` | — | replace an existing APP_KEY |
| `--show` | — | print the key instead of writing it |

### oauth:client:create

Register an OAuth client for the MCP connector.

```bash
ims oauth:client:create [flags]
```

Examples:

```bash
ims oauth:client:create --name "Ops agent" --redirect https://agent.example.com/callback --confidential
ims oauth:client:create --name "Local tool" --redirect http://localhost/callback
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--confidential` | — | give the client a secret (server-side clients) |
| `--name` | — | name shown on the consent page (required) |
| `--read-only` | — | never grant mcp:write |
| `--redirect` | — | redirect URI (repeat for more; https, or http on localhost) |
| `--tenant` | `0` | only this tenant's users may connect |

### oauth:client:delete

Delete an OAuth client and revoke every connection made with it.

```bash
ims oauth:client:delete <id>
```

### oauth:client:list

List the OAuth clients registered for the MCP connector.

```bash
ims oauth:client:list
```

### oauth:client:rotate

Give a confidential OAuth client a new secret (the old one works for MCP_OAUTH_SECRET_GRACE).

```bash
ims oauth:client:rotate <id>
```

### openapi:check

Validate the embedded OpenAPI document (api/openapi.yaml) and compare it
against the live router. Requires database connectivity (the route table is
built from the full dependency graph), like health:check.

```bash
ims openapi:check
```

### permission:sync

Sync the permission catalog into the database.

```bash
ims permission:sync
```

### privacy:coverage

List every database column that may point at a user, the module whose privacy contributor handles it or the reason it is exempt. Exits with an error when a column is not covered.

```bash
ims privacy:coverage
```

### privacy:erase

Erase a user's personal data in every module and keep the users row as a tombstone (docs/design/account-deletion-and-export.md). It cannot be undone, so it needs --force. The super admin and a tenant's last active Admin are refused.

```bash
ims privacy:erase [flags]
```

Examples:

```bash
ims privacy:erase --user=42 --force
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--force` | — | confirm the erasure (it cannot be undone) |
| `--user` | `0` | id of the user to erase |

### privacy:export

Write every module's data about a user (JSON per module, stored files, manifest.json) to a zip file. Secrets are never included.

```bash
ims privacy:export [flags]
```

Examples:

```bash
ims privacy:export --user=42 --out=user-42.zip
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--out` | — | zip file to create (default: user-<id>-export.zip; never overwritten) |
| `--user` | `0` | id of the user to export |

### privacy:ledger

Write the ids of users erased since --since (RFC 3339 date or date-time), one per line, to stdout or --out. Run it on the live database before restoring a backup, then `ims privacy:replay --from=<file>` after the restore.

```bash
ims privacy:ledger [flags]
```

Examples:

```bash
ims privacy:ledger --since=2026-11-01 --out=erased.txt
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--out` | — | file to write (default: stdout) |
| `--since` | — | erasures completed at or after this date (RFC 3339; required) |

### privacy:replay

Read user ids (one per line, from `ims privacy:ledger`) and erase every one that is not erased in this database. Users still erased or no longer present are skipped; the guards do not apply, since the erasure was already decided.

```bash
ims privacy:replay [flags]
```

Examples:

```bash
ims privacy:replay --from=erased.txt
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--from` | — | file of user ids written by privacy:ledger (required) |

### queue:stats

Show queue depths and failed counts.

```bash
ims queue:stats
```

### queue:work

Start a queue worker (River).

```bash
ims queue:work [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--max-workers` | `0` | max workers per queue (default: QUEUE_WORKER_CONCURRENCY) |
| `--once` | — | process due jobs and exit |
| `--once-timeout` | `30s` | how long --once waits for a job |
| `--queues` | — | comma-separated queues to process (default: critical,default,heavy) |

### route:list

List every HTTP route the API registers with this configuration: method, path, the
permission it requires (empty: none) and the handler. --middleware adds each route's own
middleware (after the global stack, printed at the end); --json prints the full table for
tools and AI agents. Builds the full dependency graph, like openapi:check.

```bash
ims route:list [flags]
```

Examples:

```bash
ims route:list --path=/api/v1/branch
ims route:list --method=DELETE --middleware
ims route:list --except-path=/dev --json
```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--except-path` | — | leave out routes whose path contains this text |
| `--json` | — | print the table as JSON (method, path, handler, permissions, middleware) |
| `--method` | — | only routes with this HTTP method (e.g. GET) |
| `--middleware` | — | add each route's middleware |
| `--path` | — | only routes whose path contains this text |

### two-factor:reset

Turn off two-factor authentication for the user with --email (mailed and recorded as user.two_factor_reset). Check who is asking before you run it.

```bash
ims two-factor:reset [flags]
```

Examples:

```bash

```

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--email` | — | the user's e-mail address |
